newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says EU eases sowing deadline after drought.
newsitem.headline: France says EU eases sowing deadline after drought.

text.p: The European Union's executive Commission has pushed back the deadline for declaring maize and other late grain sowings by two weeks because of recent drought, the French agriculture ministry said on Tuesday.
The deadline for maize, sorghum, soya and sunflower sowings, which traditionally come later than other crops, will be May 30 instead of May 15, it said in a statement.
Farmers also have an extra two weeks to take out contracts for industrial set-aside -- crops sown on land taken out of food production but used for alternative energy and other outlets.
The new deadline for these is May 15 instead of April 30.
France had requested the changes after farmers complained of problems caused by four months with scarcely a drop of rain.
A break in the drought since the weekend has eased crop development and sowing problems but leaves water resources needed for irrigation far below normal levels, analysts said.
